zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the puzzle, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation. Any alteration of the original text can cause a mismatch with the reference solution.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever copying attribute values into the final solution JSON.
zebralogic.example: Writing "alice" instead of "Alice" or changing "Stir Fry" to "stir fry" in the output.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "X is directly left/right of Y", enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly one in the indicated direction (X = Y − 1 for left, X = Y + 1 for right).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Processing clues that contain the phrase "directly left of" or "directly right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "X is directly left of Y" as merely "X is somewhere left of Y", allowing a gap of more than one house.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "X is somewhere to the left/right of Y", enforce a strict ordering (X < Y or X > Y) without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Processing clues that contain "somewhere left of" or "somewhere right of".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "X is somewhere left of Y" as "X must be directly left of Y", which would incorrectly forbid valid placements with a gap.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the person whose child is Alice loves cooking"), assign both values to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Processing clues that state two attributes refer to the same entity.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the child name "Alice" to one house and the cooking hobby to a different house, breaking the equivalence.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., "the doctorate is in house 1"), place that attribute in the indicated house and treat it as immutable.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Processing clues that specify an exact house number for an attribute.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the clue that the doctorate must be in house 1 and allowing it to appear elsewhere.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, quotes, and matching keys/values.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately before emitting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Producing JSON with a missing closing bracket or an extra trailing comma, causing a parse error.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier can reliably extract the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When constructing the final response after all reasoning is complete.
zebralogic.example: Appending explanatory text after the JSON, which may be cut off by the token limit and hide the solution from the verifier.

zebralogic.title: OverlappingCategoryDisambiguation
zebralogic.principle: When a value appears in multiple categories (e.g., a name also used as a child), treat each occurrence as belonging to its own category and keep the categories distinct.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a value that could belong to more than one attribute set.
zebralogic.example: Treating the child name "Alice" as the same entity as the person named Alice, leading to duplicate assignments.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B, B = C), propagate the links so all linked attributes share the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After processing all equivalence clues, run a transitive closure to merge linked groups.
zebralogic.example: Linking child = Alice to cooking but forgetting that cooking is also linked to tennis, leaving tennis unconnected.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between two entities, enforce that the absolute difference in their house numbers equals N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Processing clues that specify a numeric gap, such as "two houses between A and B".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between A and B" as a difference of 2 (placing them two houses apart) instead of the required difference of 3.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting "N houses between" as "N houses apart" (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The phrasing "two houses between" is often read as a simple offset, ignoring the houses that lie in between.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions a number of houses between two entities, add one to that number to obtain the required absolute house-number difference.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues generating reasoning after the JSON, exceeding the token limit or pushing the JSON out of the parser's view.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise and ensure the JSON object is the very last output, with no trailing characters.
